spots.name: Cathedral of St. Elizabeth
spots.summary: The Cathedral of St. Elizabeth, also called Saint Elizabeth Cathedral, is a Gothic cathedral in Košice, Slovakia. It is the largest church in Slovakia and one of the easternmost Gothic cathedrals in Europe.

spots.name: East Slovak Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: The East Slovak Museum in Košice, Slovakia, is one of the oldest Slovak museums, founded in 1872. It is located in the Old Town borough of Košice, at Námestie Maratónu mieru.

spots.name: St Michael Chapel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Saint Michael Church is a Gothic style church in Košice, Slovakia. Originally a chapel, the building became officially a church after its reconstruction in 2006.

spots.name: St. Urban Tower
spots.summary: The Urban Tower in Košice, Slovakia is a renaissance prismatic campanile with a pyramidal roof. It was erected in the 16th century.

spots.name: Plague Column, Košice
spots.summary: The Plague Column or Immaculata is a Baroque plague column in Košice, Slovakia.

spots.name: Hlavná ulica
spots.summary: Hlavná ulica is the central street of Košice, Slovakia. Most important historical monuments of Košice are located on it. The southern end of the street ends at Liberators Square, the northern end at Marathon Peace Square.

spots.name: Church of the Holy Trinity, Košice

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of the Holy Trinity or commonly known as the Premonstratensian Church, or initially the Jesuit Church, is a Roman Catholic church in Košice, Slovakia. It is an example of Baroque architecture in the city and was the site of the martyrdom of three saints in 1619.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of the Holy Trinity, Košice

spots.name: East Slovak Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The East Slovak Gallery, established in 1951, was the first regional gallery in Slovakia. The mission of the Gallery is the protection and presentation of the collection and documentation of the art scene and artistic life in the region of Eastern Slovakia.

spots.name: National Theatre Košice
spots.summary: The National Theatre Košice is situated in the centre of Košice, Slovakia.

spots.name: Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary or commonly known as the Dominican Church at Dominikánske námestie is the oldest church in Košice, Slovakia, and also the oldest preserved building in the town.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary, Košice

spots.name: Slovak Technical Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Slovak Technical Museum is a major Slovak technology museum, based in the eastern Slovak city of Košice, with branches throughout Slovakia. It was established in 1947 and opened to the public in 1948, under the name Technical Museum. The museum was renamed to its current name in 1983.

spots.name: New Orthodox Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The New Orthodox Synagogue is an Orthodox Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at Puškinova Street near the historic centre of Košice, Slovakia. The congregation worships in the Ashkenazi rite.

photo.author: Marian Gladis, Picture from English Wikipedia

spots.name: St Anthony of Padua Church, Košice

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Anthony of Padua Church or commonly known as the Franciscan Church or the Seminary Church at Hlavná ulica is the second oldest church in Košice, Slovakia.
spots.wikipediaTitle: St Anthony of Padua Church, Košice

spots.name: Archbishop's Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Archbishop's Palace of Košice, Slovakia, is a rococo-classical building, formerly the home of Austro-Hungarian Emperor Franz Joseph I.

spots.name: Church of Virgin Mary's Birth

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Greek Catholic Cathedral Church of Virgin Mary's Birth is located at Moyzesova Street in the historic centre of Košice, Slovakia. It is the cathedral of the Eparchy of Košice of the Slovak Greek Catholic Church.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Cathedral of the Nativity of the Mother of God, Košice

spots.name: Evangelical Church of Košice

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Evangelical Church or Protestant Church in Mlynská ulica in Košice, Slovakia is a Neoclassical church building of the Evangelical Church of the Augsburg Confession in Slovakia, a Lutheran denomination. It has Sunday services at 09:30 and 18:00 in Slovak, and at 08:15 in Hungarian.

spots.name: Singing fountain in Košice
spots.summary: You may find it difficult not to find the 'singing fountain' in front of the theater enjoyable on warm afternoons or evenings. Calm music tunes and accompanying water salvos provide lovely vibes for couples enjoying their ice cream and serve as a hilarious entertainment for the kids. The music "feature" of the fountain is mostly active hourly on public holidays and/or in the evenings. It was inaug

spots.summary: Baroque building from the 18th century, this palace too hosts a library.

spots.name: Levočský dom
spots.summary: The oldest house in the city. It houses a restaurant, where Gothic vaults are visible.

spots.name: Andrássy Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A three floor Neo-Baroque building constructed in 1899, with the blazon of the family on the façade. Nowadays the building houses a tea house and a restaurant.

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.name: Čáky-Dezőfi palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Count Antal Csáky had this palace built in 1807. Count Abaúj-Torna, the county governor, resided here in the 1840s, then the Dezőfi family. One of the most pompous buildings in the city, it has hosted many important guests including Russian Tsars. In 1965 the palace was turned into an art gallery, and from 1993 to 2007 the Constitutional Court of Slovakia functioned here. Nowadays it's a major lib

spots.name: Košice town hall
spots.summary: A late Baroque palace built between 1779 and 1790. In the late 1920s it was converted into a cinemand and a library, though in 1996 it was renovated and the city council returned to the building. Part of it is open to the public.

spots.name: prison of Mikluš

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: Exhibition focused on the history of the city, it's part of the East Slovak Museum. Built as two gothic houses, it became a prison and is today named after its executioner.

spots.name: Archaeological Museum in Košice

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Newly reconstructed archaeological basement of the main street at the lower gate of the 13th century fortifications of the city. Additionally you can still find parts of fortification in other places around the city center. All videos and text in the museum has English, Hungarian and Slovak description.

spots.name: Vojtech Löffler Museum

hours.note: Closed Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat

spots.summary: Likely interesting for the more art inclined traveler after seeing the usual government sponsored touristy stuff.

spots.name: Synagogue in Košice (Zvonárska)

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Built in 1883 in Moorish style, as of 2018 renovations were underway to make it a cultural center. It's the heart of the Jewish cultural community in Košice nowadays. It has a prayer room, a mikveh and a kosher café.

spots.name: Church of St. Michael the Archangel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Pongrác-Forgáč Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: An Empire style building from the early 19th century with the blazons of the Forgács and Pongrá families on the façade, now a library. In the 1940s, when a bank functioned here, a glass roof was installed, this part is now accessible to the public.

spots.name: Žobrákov dom ("House of the beggar")
spots.summary: For an interesting story you may look up the Beggar's House which is one of the historical houses on Hlavna (on the right between the Theater and Immaculata when walking up north). On forefront, at top of the house you will see a statue of a guy with a hat thanking/begging for alms. spots.name: Jakabov palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Erected in 1899 by entrepreneur Arpád Jakab in the pseudo-Gothic style constructed from discarded stones from the Kosice St. Elizabeth's Cathedral. At the end of WWII it was the residence for Czechoslovak president Edvard Beneš. Most of the inhabitants of Košice would choose this building as one of the most beautiful ones.

An alternative music and lifestyle craving types may find this one to be a great place for an entertaining hangout or a not occasional international live music act. Also a great place for partying even until the weekday wee hours. Discretion or attending in wider groups

spots.name: Jazz Club

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Despite the confusing name (no jazz music happening in there) providing for the dance music and party craving types and being the place to go for the regular night entertainment seeking locals on most week days. A bit overpriced but definitely lively. Serves food also.

spots.name: Ajvega

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A vegetarian and celiac diet friendly meals and pizzas providing restaurant. Dietary meals (with some including meat) offered at the 'tower', upstairs. A quiet place with a terrace enjoyable on warmer days. A weekday inexpensive midday lunch menu offered.

spots.name: Beer House

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Beer House offers probably the widest range of beers in the city. The cheapest beer is for €1.06/0.5l, most expensive €1.96/0.5l. They offer pizza at the same time and you can order it until 2am. There is live music every Thursday and Saturday.

spots.name: Camelot

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Pub with a Medieval theme, traditional food such as pork knuckle or goulash, with quality beef from a known local supplier. Unpasteurised Pilsner Urquell on tap. A bit expensive but they have lunch specials on week days.

spots.name: Caffé Trieste

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Italian-style café part of a chain. The chain has three other cafés in Košice: at Žriedlová 11 west of old town, at Trieda SNP 395/37 further west and at Južna trieda 2/A south of old town.

spots.name: Pizzeria Zvon

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Lovely pizza restaurant, with great food, was about €5.20 for a large pizza. All stone baked on hand thrown dough, brilliant toppings, lively atmosphere, and great staff.

spots.name: Golem

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Nice pub and restaurant with an indulging vibe usually on all week days. Try out their own microbrewery produced beers and home made pickled ermine cheese.

spots.name: Bistro Záhrada

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Another popular Slovak-style "Biergarten", a nice place to sit on a warm summer evening. During wintertime it's a small bar in a basement with boardgames.
